title: Reasons to stay natural: you pay PED use with your lifespan
summary: Argues that PEDs essentially buy time: they add artificial 'tonnage' that would take impossible amounts of training to match, and the price is paid in years of lifespan. Size gained on drugs disappears when they stop, and users who never learned to train go back on, shaving years off the end of their life. Natural training is slower but builds discipline, knowledge and health you keep.

claims.claim: Most people jumping on PEDs know vaguely about health complications but don't grasp that they are making a real sacrifice.
PEDs 'speed time up': they let you accomplish in a short time what would take a natural far longer, or forever.

Some physiques are impossible for naturals both because PEDs change the hormonal profile beyond any natural and because they add so much artificial tonnage that the lifting time needed to match it is unattainable.
You pay for PEDs with your lifespan: the hours you skipped in the gym are paid back as years in the coffin.
PEDs essentially add tonnage without lifting, which is why people get big on them with little training and why body parts grow without isolation work.
The so-called natural limit is really a time limit: eventually it takes so much work to reach the tonnage needed to keep growing that people decide it's not worth it.
PEDs could be equivalent to adding 100-200 hours of training per week, which explains the insane results especially when combined with training.
When a natural stops training, muscle shrinks because it's no longer challenged by the tonnage; when a PED user stops, the artificially applied tonnage disappears and the size goes with it.

Although regaining size has been shown to be slightly easier after PED use, he argues naturals regain size more easily in practice because they have the discipline and knowledge of how to train it back.
People who got big through drugs rather than training never learned to rebuild with training, so they go back on and never stop.
Every cycle shaves years off the end of your life; you may feel fine in your 20s-40s, but by the time the damage shows it's too late.
Being natural is better because even if the muscle leaves you, the training made you healthier and stronger, letting you enjoy your later years with family.
Better to taste the pain of discipline early than to see a chunk of your life disappear; lifting is a long run and you need to live long for that.
Building a good physique naturally is possible but takes hard work, discipline, experience, study and thinking.
